title: Password Reuse Across Accounts and Systems
description: The same or similar passwords are reused across multiple accounts, systems, or privilege levels (for example, a local administrator password shared across many hosts, or staff reusing corporate passwords on external services). Compromise of one credential therefore cascades to many systems, and credential-stuffing of breached passwords becomes effective.
businessImpact: High --- a single compromised password can grant access to numerous systems, dramatically expanding the blast radius of any breach and enabling lateral movement.
remediation:
- Enforce unique passwords per account and per privilege tier.
- Deploy a solution such as LAPS to randomize and rotate local administrator passwords per host.
- Screen new passwords against known-breached password lists.
- Enforce multi-factor authentication, especially for privileged and remote access.
- Provide a password manager and user education.
